the efficiency of simultaneous evaluations is 15 to 20% better than the efficiency of separate (Northeast region) mixed model evaluations.
simultaneous genetic evaluations of the dam, sire, maternal grandsire are 95% as efficient as separate genetic evaluations of cows and bulls in predicting the genetic merit of progeny of the cows.

simultaneous genetic evaluations are more efficient than separate (Northeast region) genetic evaluations for predicting genetic evaluations in progeny of Holstein cows in the northeastern United States.

the use of mixed model procedures for genetic evaluation of bulls, cows, and progeny.

the development of a genetic evaluation procedure for dairy bulls and cows that will provide genetic evaluations for progeny that are at least as efficient as those obtained from separate evaluations of dams, sires, and maternal grandsires.
the use of mixed model methodology to estimate genetic parameters and to predict genetic merit of animals in the presence of all available information on relationships among animals.

the simultaneous genetic evaluation procedures were more efficient than the separate genetic evaluation procedures for predicting progeny evaluations.

the simultaneous genetic evaluation procedure is more efficient than the separate genetic evaluation procedure for predicting progeny genetic evaluations from dam, sire and maternal grandsire genetic evaluations.
